knowledge:
- key_parameters: ngenes=Vector of integers specifying the number of genes/features to select and evaluate ;; ntrain=Size of the training set (or "balanced" to ensure equal representation of classes) ;; method=Feature selection method used in fit (e.g., "welch.test") ;; positive=The class label representing the positive outcome (e.g., "DM") ;; dist=Distance metric for nearest-centroid classification in predict (options: "euclidean", "center", "angle", "cor") ;; score=Prediction score calculation method in plot (options: "z", "zeta", "ratio") ;; type=Plot type for prediction results (options: "histogram", "roc", "logistic")
- alternatives: The documentation notes that simple classifiers (like nearest-centroid) often perform as well as or better than more sophisticated methods on high-dimensional data, citing Wessels et al.
- when_to_use: Use when developing and validating diagnostic or prognostic classifiers from high-dimensional molecular data (e.g., microarray gene expression datasets) where overfitting is a concern and robust validation (like multiple random validation) is required.
- pitfalls: Overfitting and performance overestimation due to high dimensionality and multiple testing. Computational intensity: running multiple random validation protocols on very large feature sets can be slow, so reducing the feature space or using subsetted data during initial testing is recommended.

workflows.name: multiple_random_validation
workflows.intent: Evaluate classification accuracy and estimate misclassification rates across different numbers of genes or training set sizes using a multiple random validation protocol.
input: ExpressionSet (high-dimensional molecular data with class labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Run multiple random validation across different gene counts using nvalidate ;; 2. Plot misclassification rates using plot ;; 3. Run validation across different training set sizes using validate ;; 4. Plot training size validation results using plot
workflows.code:
nval <- nvalidate(GOLUB1[1:200, ], ngenes=c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200))
plot(nval)
val <- validate(GOLUB1[1:200, ], ngenes=10, ntrain="balanced")
plot(val)

workflows.name: predictor_construction_and_independent_validation
workflows.intent: Fit a nearest-centroid predictor on a training dataset and predict/evaluate outcomes on an independent validation dataset.
input: ExpressionSet (independent validation dataset with class labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit a predictor on the training dataset using fit ;; 2. Predict classes and calculate continuous scores on the validation dataset using predict ;; 3. Plot score distribution histogram using plot(..., type="histogram") ;; 4. Plot ROC curve using plot(..., type="roc") ;; 5. Fit and plot a logistic regression model using plot(..., type="logistic")
workflows.code:
predictor <- fit(VEER, method="welch.test")
prediction <- predict(predictor, VIJVER2, positive="DM", dist="cor")
plot(prediction, type="histogram", positive="DM", score="zeta")
plot(prediction, type="roc", positive="DM", score="zeta")
plot(prediction, type="logistic", positive="DM", score="zeta")
